note: Source validated against the official Kumon UK and Singapore curricula (2026). Maths: levels 7A to O plus the X specialty tracks (XV Vectors, XM Transformations, XP Permutations, XS Statistics). English: 18 main levels 7A to L, with sub levels AI/AII through GI/GII for levels A to G. H to L are single levels. The final English level is L.
warning: This roadmap is maintained by hand and can lag behind the real worksheet content. Check it against the current week before trusting it.
granularity: Levels A to D of maths are broken down by Kumon sheet set, because that is where both children are working. From Level E up, and for English above Level D, each level lists the published topics for that level rather than its sheet sets. Check a level with the centre before treating its breakdown as exact.
stateNote: A level is marked current when at least one sub-topic inside it is. More than one level can be current at once: the weekly homework runs nine slots in parallel, so multiplication and division can advance on different sheets. Every current sub-topic names the homework slot and rung that evidences it, from data/curriculum/position.json on 2026-10-11. For tracks.nsw, `current` means the child's recorded rung delivers that family THIS week, not that a slot is heading for it. `kh.py validate` derives the same set from the spine and refuses a push when the two disagree, in either direction.
shapeNote: The two ladders below are the Kumon programme itself, so they are defined once and shared. A child record holds only where that child stands on them: every id in `cleared`, every id in `current` with the reason, and everything else is still ahead. That is deliberate. The two children were previously two hand kept copies of the same ladder, which is how a roadmap drifts.

sections.label: Reading
sections.sub: Selective: 17 questions, 38 answers, 45 minutes. OC: 14 questions, 40 minutes. Five distinct item types, not one comprehension task.

items.name: Paired extracts, compared
items.detail: Two short texts on one theme, then multiple choice on both: which extract does X, why a detail matters, what the writer implies, how the writer feels. Items 1 to 8 of the real paper.

items.name: Vocabulary in context
items.detail: A passage with gaps. Each gap offers four near synonyms and only one fits the register and collocation: ordaining / inaugurating / consecrating / enthroning. 8 answers.

items.name: Poetry
items.detail: A poem, then questions on what the title does, what is compared to what, which word use is the odd one out, and what the form of the poem reflects.

items.name: Missing sentences
items.detail: Six sentences are removed from a text and seven are offered. Each gap is filled by tracking reference words and the thread of the argument.

items.name: Four extracts, matched to statements
items.detail: Four extracts on one theme and ten statements: which extract mentions, argues, describes, explains this. Scanning four texts at once against a claim.

sections.label: Mathematical Reasoning
sections.sub: Selective and OC: 35 questions, 40 minutes, five options each, no calculator. Concepts from the NSW curriculum to Year 6 for selective, to Year 4 for OC.

items.name: Place value and rounding
items.detail: Numbers to millions, what a digit represents, how many times larger one digit's value is than another's, and comparing two different roundings of the same number.

items.name: Multiples, factors and counting
items.detail: Largest multiple under a limit, how many numbers in a range are multiples of 3 but not of 8, smallest and largest possible values under two conditions.

items.name: Fractions of a quantity
items.detail: Fractions of a shape and of an amount, comparing and combining unlike fractions, sharing a whole between four people and finding the difference.

items.name: Working backwards
items.detail: He gave half of what was left, then half of that, and the last person got $1.60. Undoing a chain of operations, and choosing the number sentence that models a situation.

items.name: Measurement and scale reading
items.detail: Grams, millilitres, metres and centimetres converted inside one question, a jar weighed with its contents, and a scale whose pointer does not start at zero.

items.name: Time, 24 hour and time zones
items.detail: 1850 in 12 hour format, a duration that crosses midnight, and a journey through two flights and a 17 hour time difference.

items.name: Area and perimeter of composite shapes
items.detail: Perimeter of a shape left when two rectangles are cut from one, equal areas giving an unknown side, and the black area of a part shaded figure.

items.name: Shape, angle and symmetry
items.detail: Lines of symmetry, the angle in a symmetrical figure, rotation through a given angle, cube nets, views from the side, and faces plus edges plus vertices of a hexagonal pyramid.

items.name: Probability
items.detail: Probability as a decimal or fraction, the remaining probability when two are given, and judging three probability statements at once.

items.name: Graphs and tables
items.detail: A rainfall column graph and a temperature line graph, each with three statements to test, including one that needs a unit change from centimetres to metres.

items.name: Patterns and two unknowns
items.detail: Each term is the sum of the three before it, a magic square with gaps, and 3 stars plus 5 hearts is 27 points while 5 stars plus 7 hearts is 41.

items.name: Rate and best value
items.detail: Two pack sizes and a quantity to hit exactly, cheapest valid combination, and which shop to buy from.

sections.label: Thinking Skills
sections.sub: Selective: 40 questions, 40 minutes. OC: 30 questions, 30 minutes. Four options. Deliberately no curriculum knowledge: it is argument analysis, logic and spatial reasoning.

items.name: Strengthen an argument
items.detail: Someone makes a case. Which statement, if true, most strengthens it. The commonest single item type on the paper.

items.name: Weaken an argument
items.detail: The same shape in reverse: which statement, if true, most weakens the argument.

items.name: Spot the mistake in reasoning
items.detail: Two people talk and one draws a bad conclusion. Which sentence shows the mistake: usually a confusion of necessary with sufficient, or treating one case as all cases.

items.name: Conditional reasoning
items.detail: If only those at the meeting may go on the excursion, what follows and what does not. Must be true, cannot be true, whose reasoning is correct.

items.name: Constraint puzzles
items.detail: Five children's ages from four clues, who stands where in a row, the minimum final score that guarantees the prize.

items.name: Spatial and visual reasoning
items.detail: Which piece completes the shape, which view is possible from the side, which arrangement cannot be made, and a seven segment display with two broken segments.

items.name: Deduction from data
items.detail: A table or chart that does not state the answer: how many goats had one kid only, how many owners had exactly one dog, which category was left out.

items.name: Cost and optimisation
items.detail: Several offers and a constraint, and the cheapest or best combination has to be found rather than calculated directly.

items.name: Calendar and scheduling
items.detail: A show runs from the 12th to the 29th with extra matinees on two weekdays. Counting events over a date range without slipping by one.

items.name: What evidence would settle it
items.detail: Which two of the missing answers must be known in order to test whether the claim is true.

sections.label: Writing
sections.sub: Selective only: one task, 30 minutes, typed. Not part of the OC test.

items.name: Writing to a brief
items.detail: The task names an audience and a text type, such as an advice sheet for three new students, and the response has to actually be that text type.

items.name: Persuasive writing
items.detail: A position held consistently, reasons ordered by strength, and the obvious objection answered.

items.name: Imaginative writing
items.detail: A narrative or descriptive response to a prompt, shaped rather than merely started.

items.name: Planning under 30 minutes
items.detail: Three or four minutes of planning, then a finished piece inside the remaining time. The paper gives space for notes and says to think about organisation first.

items.name: Typing the response
items.detail: The writing test is typed on a department computer, so handwriting speed is irrelevant and typing speed and on screen editing are not.
